sources.claim: NVIDIA documents free hosted NIM API access for Developer Program prototyping, research, development and testing, while production use requires AI Enterprise.
The current model page labels a free prototype endpoint and shows integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1.
HTTP 402 remains reserved for future use; universal retry or scope semantics cannot be inferred from the RFC.
HTTP 429 specifically represents rate limiting and may carry Retry-After, distinguishing it from the project's conservative 402 payment fence.
HTTPError is both an exception and a file-like HTTP response with a code, so both runtime transport shapes require explicit tests.

evidence_families.fusion: Official free-prototyping documentation supports provider discovery but cannot attest the entitlement, remaining credits, billing principal or zero-cost status of a concrete credential at execution time. The nonretryable 402 rule is therefore a project safety policy, not an RFC guarantee.

concepts.hypothesis: Cost authorization and payment-state receipts must bind an opaque control-plane identity for <provider, credential/account principal, project, endpoint origin, model or product, entitlement/pricing evidence version, budget epoch>; semantic request equality alone cannot authorize a retry.
concepts.counterhypothesis: Provider-wide identity is safer and sufficient because finer scoping can accidentally route around a paid boundary through another account, model or endpoint.
concepts.synthesis: On an untyped or ambiguous 402, fail closed provider-wide for the current cycle. Narrow the fence only when provider-specific, verified error semantics prove a smaller cost scope. Never serialize a secret or an unsalted raw-key hash; use a host-held opaque handle or keyed pseudonym.
decisive_tests: Execute the same provider/host/body fixture under two injected allowed credential handles; require one semantic digest but distinct cost-principal and execution lineages.
Rotate the credential/account/project binding and require the receipt lineage to change without exposing secret material.
For an unknown 402 scope, assert that every same-provider route is refused before network in the current cycle.
Permit narrower recovery only with a typed provider-specific fixture that proves model/project scope and is separately policy-reviewed.

concepts.hypothesis: Receipts need separate semantic_request_id and cost_authority_id/execution_lineage_id: retries of identical content under one authority preserve the semantic ID, while authority changes create a new execution lineage and require fresh authorization.
concepts.counterhypothesis: One request ID is operationally simpler and adequate if retries never switch credentials or accounts.
concepts.falsifier: If every production router can prove a credential/account/project invariant from authorization through all retries and fallbacks, the second identity adds no safety information.
decisive_tests: Same payload plus same principal: stable semantic ID, unique attempt IDs, stable cost-authority ID.
Same payload plus different principal: stable semantic ID is allowed, but cost-authority and execution-lineage IDs must differ and rerouting requires authorization.
Crash/restart replay must restore both identities without permitting a retry under a different unrecorded principal.

concepts.hypothesis: FREE_ONLY payment state must be monotonic within a budget epoch: ELIGIBLE may become PAYMENT_UNKNOWN_OR_REQUIRED and then INELIGIBLE_CURRENT_CYCLE; a cooldown timer must never silently restore eligibility after 402.
concepts.counterhypothesis: A short cooldown is appropriate where a provider uses 402 transiently or at model scope.
concepts.synthesis: Default to a persisted provider-wide latch because RFC 9110 leaves 402 semantics undefined; override only through typed, provider-specific evidence and an explicit policy rule.
decisive_tests: Cover both regular-response 402 and HTTPError(402); require PAYMENT_REQUIRED_HARD_STOP, EXECUTED but never VERIFIED/DONE, zero retry permission.
Attempt the same provider twice in one cycle; after the first 402 the second opener/network call count must remain zero.
Restart the runtime within the same budget epoch and prove the latch survives.
Advance the budget epoch only through an explicit host-side authorization event, never elapsed cooldown alone.
